0xabys/saigon-rush-hour.readme:
# Saigon Rush Hour

An isometric 3D traffic simulator of District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, running in the browser — Three.js + TypeScript + Vite.

**Live demo:** https://0xabys.github.io/saigon-rush-hour/

About 80.5 % of vehicles are two-wheelers (motorbikes plus Grab/Be/Xanh SM ride-hailing bikes, ~30 % of which are ride-hailing) and ~14.7 % are cars (including taxis and Xanh SM/Grab Car/Be Car ride-hailing cars, ~45 % of which are ride-hailing). The bikes flow like water around cars, buses, Vinasun/Mai Linh taxis and cyclos. The car share follows the latest 2025 HCMC figures (≈ 1.4 M cars / 11.3 M motorbikes registered as of 08/2025, plus 102,354 cars and 290,570 motorbikes newly registered in 2025 per the Traffic Police Department → ≈ 11.2 % cars at end of 2025) plus taxis. The ride-hailing split is an assumption based on street observation (no published counts exist for District 1). Congestion level and speeds are checked against the TomTom Traffic Index 2025.

## Running

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm run build      # typecheck + bundle into dist/
npm run preview    # serve the build
```

Requires a browser with WebGL2 (recent Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari).

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| Left / right drag, scroll | Rotate / pan / zoom the camera |
| Click a vehicle | Follow it and show its info card |
| Click a road (**Tuyến đường** tab) | Show hourly density and average speed |
| `Space` · `1` `2` `4` | Pause · speed ×1 ×2 ×4 |
| `R` | Toggle rain (slippery roads, flooding) |
| `T` | Time machine — rewind the last 60 simulated seconds |
| `F` · `Esc` | Follow a random vehicle · stop following |
| `H` | Show/hide the control panel |

The in-app UI is in Vietnamese.

## What's simulated

- **Driving models**: cars, taxis, buses and trucks use the **IDM** (Intelligent Driver Model) — free-road acceleration, time-gap keeping, smooth braking behind the leader. **Motorbikes** use a **social force model**: attraction towards open gaps ahead plus anisotropic exponential repulsion (front-weighted) from nearby vehicles, pedestrians, kerbs and the centre line; IDM only acts as a safety brake against the vehicle directly ahead.
- **Driver personalities**: each vehicle has its own **aggressiveness**, **caution** and **desired speed**, seeded from its id (ride-hailing bikes and buses are pushier; cyclos are the gentlest). Personality changes the IDM parameters (acceleration, time gap, standstill gap, braking), the personal space in the social force model and the patience when entering roundabouts. The vehicle card shows the personality and desired speed.
- **Saigon style** (the more aggressive, the more often): **briefly riding against traffic** before cutting back (yielding to oncoming vehicles), **riding on the sidewalk** when stuck for long, **stopping past the stop line** at red lights (bikes spill over the line, some cars poke their nose out), **running the red when the countdown shows 1–2 s**, **pushing through amber**, **honking** ("•••" bubbles) — aggressive drivers also honk at slow vehicles ahead. Bikes **squeeze into junctions** as soon as there is space at the exit (no need for the whole exit to be clear); vehicles **waiting on side streets force their way in** — the longer they wait, the smaller the gap they accept, and cars on the main road leave room for them.
- **Trips & routing**: vehicles don't just cross between two map edges — some start **mid-block** and end **inside the network** (pull over and leave), especially on commercial streets such as Nguyễn Huệ, Lê Lợi, Đồng Khởi and Lê Thánh Tôn. At each turn, drivers pick a direction by **real-time cost** (remaining distance + congestion on each branch, softmax weighted by personality), so traffic spills onto quieter streets when an artery jams.
- **Traffic lights** with countdown timers; right turn on red is allowed except where signed otherwise. From **23:00 to 05:00** lights switch to **flashing amber** and the countdowns go dark: vehicles slow down, enter only when no cross traffic is moving through, and whoever has waited longest goes first (reckless bikers skip the yielding). The “Khuya” button jumps to 23:30.
- **Pedestrians crossing**: on zebra crossings when their direction has a red light, and “Saigon style” — conical hat on, walking slowly and steadily through traffic mid-block. Every vehicle must yield; bikes weave around, cars stop and wait (the vehicle card says it is yielding to a pedestrian).
- **Events**: minor crashes (vehicles block a lane with traffic cones, followers slow down to look and go around); **flooding** at real low spots on Tôn Đức Thắng, Hàm Nghi, Lê Lai, Pasteur and Calmette during heavy rain — muddy water rises over ~30 s and drains ~90 s after the rain stops (vehicles crawl, some stall and get pushed); **truck ban** in the inner city 6–9h and 16–20h (signs at every map entry).

cktang88/3d-fps.readme:
# IRONLINE — realistic browser FPS

A tactical first-person shooter that runs in the browser: **three.js r186** rendering, **Rapier** physics,
**Recast/Detour** navigation for bots, **pmndrs/postprocessing + N8AO** for the image pipeline and an
**AMD FSR 1** upscaler.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
npm run build    # static build in dist/
```

![Team deathmatch in the courtyard](docs/screenshots/action.jpg)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Golden-hour sun over the office block](docs/screenshots/sun.jpg) | ![Warehouse interior under sodium lamps](docs/screenshots/warehouse.jpg) |
| *Low storm sun, god rays and wet asphalt* | *Warehouse: practical lamps, light shafts, dust* |
| ![Warehouse catwalk](docs/screenshots/catwalk.jpg) | ![Container yard](docs/screenshots/containers.jpg) |
| *Catwalk over the racking* | *Container yard after the rain* |

*In-engine captures at 1600x900, High quality (no post-edit).*

## Requirements & performance

- A WebGL2 browser with hardware acceleration on. **Chrome** (or another Chromium browser) is recommended and
  is what the game is tested on.
- First boot picks graphics settings from the GPU (`Renderer.autoQuality`): discrete GPUs get **High + FSR Quality**,
  Apple Silicon and integrated GPUs (Intel Iris/UHD, Radeon APUs) get **Medium + FSR Balanced**, software renderers and
  phones get **Low + FSR Performance**. On Apple GPUs the automatic setting also turns off the viewmodel light probe
  (a GPU→CPU readback) and the viewmodel shadow pass, which stall Metal's tile-based GPUs. Picking a quality or
  upscaling mode yourself turns this off.
- **Adaptive quality**: while the quality is still automatic, a machine that averages under 30 fps steps one feature
  down at a time (AO → god rays → shadow map → viewmodel probe → bloom → render scale) and shows a toast. It never steps
  back up by itself; picking a quality in Settings resets it.
- **Graphics benchmark**: Settings → Video → *Run graphics benchmark*. It replays a fixed 5-view camera tour once per
  step, turning one feature off per step, and reports frame ms (mean / p95), main-thread ms, GPU ms per pass (where
  `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2` exists), draw calls and shader programs. *Copy results* gives a plain-text table
  for bug reports.
- Budgets and measurements: [`docs/PERF.md`](docs/PERF.md).

## Features

- **Map**: *Ironline Depot*, an abandoned industrial compound at the edge of a live war zone: warehouse with catwalks
  and racks, two-storey office, container yard, western ruins and guard tower, central courtyard. Stormy golden hour
  after rain, with distant artillery, flares, smoke columns, burning wrecks, drizzle, lightning and helicopter
  fly-bys.
- **Movement** (Source-style accel/friction): walk, sprint, **tactical sprint** (double-tap Shift, limited stamina),
  crouch, **slide** (crouch while sprinting), jump, **vault** over low cover, **mantle** onto ledges (also from the
  air), lean Q/E, slow walk (Alt, silent), fall damage. **Full-body awareness**: your own legs and shadow
  (`PlayerBody.js`).
- **Camera feel**: eased recoil kick, trauma-based shake, head bob from mocap-derived curves (`CamCurves.js`), landing
  dip, lean/slide roll, sprint FOV, ADS zoom with zoom-relative sensitivity. *Reduce camera motion* scales it down.
- **Weapons (11)**: M4A1 and AK-47 (assault rifles), SCAR-L (battle rifle), MP5A5 (SMG), VSS Vintorez (marksman SMG),
  RPK-74 (LMG, drum), M870 MCS (pump shotgun), M24 SWS and AWM .338 (bolt-action), P226 and M1911A1 (pistols).
  Fire modes auto / burst / semi / pump / bolt (per weapon), sprint-to-fire delay, **tactical vs empty reloads**
  (+1 in the chamber, reload cancel before the commit point), shell-by-shell shotgun loading, bolt cycling, inspect,
  melee (backstabs kill), cookable frag grenades.
- **Recoil** (`Recoil.js`, research in [`docs/RECOIL_RESEARCH.md`](docs/RECOIL_RESEARCH.md)): per-weapon climb and
  drift profiles that move your real aim; nothing returns during a string, so you pull down. A single tap settles back
  to the point of aim, longer strings only partly. Spread bloom, stance and movement modifiers, bipod bracing.
  Bots use the same recoil and control it according to difficulty.
- **Gunsmith** (menu, or T while dead): optics (iron sights, red dot, holographic, 3.5x picture-in-picture combat
  scope, 8x sniper scope with 4x/8x zoom, glint and hold-breath), muzzle (suppressor, compensator, flash hider, brake),
  long/short barrel, vertical/angled grip, bipod, extended/fast mags, tac laser, all with live stat bars and TTK.
- **First-person presentation**: per-weapon rigs (gloved arms skinned to each gun, built offline in Blender, see
  [`docs/FP_FRAMING.md`](docs/FP_FRAMING.md)) with an authored rifle animation set (idle, walk, sprint carry, fire,
  reload, equip), hand-authored reload choreography (`ReloadChoreo.js`) with the magazine in the support hand, IK for
  the support arm, pistol slide/flip springs, inspect animations.

WollyMonjac/ButchGraves3D.readme:
# BUTCH GRAVES 3D *An experiment: can Claude Opus 5.5 build a complete game for twenty-year-old phones?*

The target was not a tech demo but a whole game: a Duke Nukem 3D–style shooter for the Java (J2ME) phones of the mid-2000s, with episodes, bosses, cutscenes, music and voices. The platform is MIDP 2.0 / CLDC 1.0, with keypad controls and screens from 128×128 to 240×320. It has no floating point, a few megabytes of memory at best, a 1 MB JAR limit on many phones, and audio firmware that is famously fragile. A human gave the brief and the direction (for example, a fifth episode in an Indiana Jones–style jungle, with a foggy night level like Silent Hill), played the builds and reported what was wrong. Claude did everything else: it wrote the game, and made every level, picture, tune and voice with tools it wrote for the job. It worked in a Linux cloud sandbox with no phone, so it also had to build its own ways to see and test what it made. ## What came out A Halloween shooter in five episodes, each ending with a boss and an animated cutscene. | Episode | Setting | Boss | |---|---|---| | 1. Night of the Pumpkin King | A cemetery, a haunted manor and catacombs | The Pumpkin King | | 2. Carnival of Carnage | A carnival of killer clowns | Mister Giggles | | 3. Bite Night | A bayou, a mad lab and a vampire's castle | Count Hollowfang | | 4. Voltage of the Damned | A robot factory on Halloween 2099 | Frankenstein Prime | | 5. Curse of the Jade Skull | Jungle temples, and a mission town lost in fog | Seven Death |

In numbers: - 20 levels, 17 monster types, 5 bosses and 5 weapons. - Over 300 rendered sprites, 25 music tracks, 56 sound effects and 88 voice lines. - About 7,000 lines of Java for the game, 13,000 lines of Python for the tools that made its levels, art and audio, and 5,000 lines of tests. - A 1.7 MB JAR, and a lite build without the voices that fits under 1 MB. ## How the art was made There is no drawn or downloaded art in the game. Every image comes out of Python scripts in `tools/`. **Monsters, weapons, props and Butch** are 3D models written as code, then rendered into sprites, much as Doom's artists photographed clay models. - **The models** are built from simple shapes: spheres, ellipsoids, boxes, cones, cylinders and tori. The shapes are blended into each other with smooth unions and carved with subtractions. Noise is pushed into their surfaces for wrinkles, bark and rot. A ghoul is made of 76 shapes, and Seven Death, the last boss, of 130. - **Materials** take their colour from 3D noise (skin, cloth, rust, bone) and can glow. Glowing parts, such as eyes, fire and the jack-o'-lantern faces, stay bright in the dark in the game. - **The renderer** is a small ray marcher that Claude wrote in numpy (`tools/sdf.py`). It lights every model with a warm key light that casts soft shadows, a cold moonlight rim and an orange glow from below. It adds ambient occlusion in the creases and supersamples the edges. - **Each monster** gets two walking frames plus attack, pain, falling and dead frames. When a monster dies, its glowing eyes go dark. - **For the cutscenes**, the villains and Butch are also rendered as big close-up portraits, with two mouth positions so they can "talk". The first-person guns and Butch's hands are rendered the same way, from a camera at eye height. **Textures and skies** are procedural 64×64 tiles that wrap seamlessly: stone blocks, mossy temple walls, rusted metal, circus stripes, circuit boards, lava and rivers. They are made from tileable noise and brick and plank generators, with signs lettered in a font. - **Opus.** Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, effort xhigh) in Claude Code, given the brief and a data

- **Fable.** Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`, effort xhigh) on the same prompt, in its own copy of
  the same empty project.

Each AI build was one unattended run from one prompt. The same scorer measured all three builds against the

The web builds run in the browser. Click the page to capture the mouse, then:

- WASD to walk, the mouse to look, Shift to run;

- M for the map;

so many rooms would otherwise be dark. The light is added when the page loads; the scenes themselves are

flakeer/poker-trainer.readme:
# Poker — an offline Texas Hold’em learning lab

https://flakeer.github.io/poker-trainer/  PLAY IT HERE

> **Vibe-coded with Claude Sonnet 5.5.** Built as a hands-on experiment in using AI to create a playable poker game and a place to learn poker by making decisions, testing ideas, and reviewing the reasoning afterward.

Poker is a browser-based Texas Hold’em trainer and AI-versus-AI sandbox. It runs locally, needs no account or backend, and uses no real money.

The goal isn't to teach you to blindly copy a bot. It's to help you build your own poker reasoning: *What hands could my opponent have? What are the pot odds? How much equity do I have? Is this decision profitable in the long run?*

## Why this project exists

I wanted more than a basic poker game. I wanted a personal poker laboratory where I could:

- Play hands and make my own decisions instead of following a scripted lesson.
- Learn poker concepts progressively, from the rules through equity, pot odds, expected value, bluffing, and advanced ideas.
- Compare my decisions with a coach's recommendation, then examine the reasoning.
- Watch AI opponents play one another with every card visible.
- Experiment with an offline AI and inspect how its decisions are made.

This is an experimental learning project—not a claim to have built a perfect poker solver.

## What you can do

### Trainer mode
Practice with a text-based coach that recommends an action and explains its reasoning. You can disagree with the recommendation. The purpose is to understand *why* a decision may be good, bad, or close—not to match the AI every time.

### Gauntlet mode
Play without coaching hints against AI opponents that adapt to observed tendencies. Decisions are timed, making this a more demanding way to test what you've learned.

### Spectate mode
Watch AI opponents play each other with all hole cards revealed. This is useful for observing hands and comparing different AI personalities.

### 12-level learning roadmap
The roadmap builds from fundamentals toward more advanced decision-making:

1. Hold’em fundamentals
2. Position
3. Starting hands and ranges
4. Pot odds
5. Equity
6. Range + equity + pot odds
7. Expected value (EV)
8. Value betting and bluffing
9. Postflop strategy
10. Reading opponents
11. Implied and reverse implied odds
12. Advanced concepts

Lessons use questions and poker situations so you can decide first and inspect the reasoning afterward.

### Progress and table features
- Session and lifetime statistics, hand history, mistake log, XP, badges, daily streaks, and leaderboard
- Synthesized sound effects and animated table feedback
- Responsive layout, including a side panel on wide screens
- A standalone HTML build that can be shared as a single file

## Decision quality matters more than the result

Poker has variance. A correct decision can lose a hand, and a poor decision can get lucky.

The trainer's review is designed to consider the decision rather than simply reward a win or punish a loss. Treat its analysis as a learning aid, not an infallible verdict: poker decisions depend on assumptions about opponents' ranges, available information, and the model's approximations.

## How the AI works

The project contains separate components for game rules, equity estimation, a fixed tight-aggressive trainer strategy, adaptive opponent behavior, and decision review. The equity engine uses Monte Carlo simulation and ranges to estimate equity; the opponents use heuristics and observed tendencies to choose actions.

**This is not a solver-grade, perfectly balanced, or guaranteed-winning AI.** Its recommendations are estimates produced by the project's models and assumptions. The code is intended to be explored, tested, and improved.

The game is designed to keep private information private during normal play: an opponent should only act on information available from its seat. Spectate mode deliberately reveals all hole cards for observation.

## Play locally

No installation, server, account, or network connection is required to play the standalone build.

1. Download or clone this repository.
2. Open `index.html` in a modern browser.

You can also open `dist/poker.html`, a self-contained build that includes the CSS and JavaScript in one file.

## Development

The project uses plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The scripts are classic browser scripts loaded in the order listed in `index.html`; several core modules can also be loaded as Node modules.

### Project layout

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Page structure and script loading |
| `css/style.css` | Styling, layout, and animation |
| `js/engine.js` | Dealing, betting, showdown, and pot rules |
| `js/equity.js` | Monte Carlo equity estimation and preflop ranges |
| `js/trainer.js` | Fixed tight-aggressive trainer strategy |
| `js/ai.js` | Adaptive AI opponents |
| `js/review.js` | Decision review and result classification |
| `js/vex.js` | Coach wording and personality |
| `js/stats.js` | Sessi

0xInsiderhq/wild-fields-1648.readme:
# Wild Fields 1648

A real-time strategy game set on the Ukrainian steppe in 1648, written by Claude Opus 5.5 and played in one browser tab. Raise a Cossack town, farm, fell forests, quarry stone, mine gold, train pikemen, musketeers, Cossack horse and field guns, and burn the rival town halls before they burn yours.

**[Play it in your browser](https://0xinsiderhq.github.io/wild-fields-1648/)** · desktop, give it a few seconds to load the scans · follow the build on X [@0xInsiderf5](https://x.com/0xInsiderf5)

![Wild Fields 1648, a regiment marching through a Cossack village](media/preview.webp)

## What is in it

- People on a jointed rig with two-bone IK, foot planting, gaits for walking, running and galloping horses, corpses that fall the right way
- Wheat that grows and ripens, paths that wear into the ground where peasants keep walking, trees that fall and leave stumps
- 25 photo-scanned models and PBR textures from Poly Haven (CC0), cut 40 to 60 times, 112 MB of downloads down to about 9 MB
- AI opponents that build, gather, research and attack; a 20 minute AI vs AI match runs without errors
- Burnt buildings leave ruins (log cribs, stone walls, a brick stove), new buildings clear the bushes on their plot
- Sound synthesised in code, no samples

## From the first build to v3

The first build had procedural models only. v3 added 25 Poly Haven scans that Claude found and downloaded itself by driving a browser, after its sandbox could not reach the asset sites.

![v1 vs v3](media/post_before_after.jpg)

## Run it locally

The page loads `assets/` with plain script and image tags, so any static server works:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# open http://localhost:8000/
```

`dist/Wild_Fields_1648_offline.html` is the same game as one 12 MB file with every scan and texture inline. It opens straight from disk.

## Build

```bash
python3 build.py
```

`src/` holds the game as plain JavaScript modules (`core`, `map`, `entities`, `ai`, `game` for the simulation, `r_*` for rendering, `ui`, `audio`, `main`). `build.py` concatenates them in a fixed order into `src/shell.html` and writes `index.html` and the offline file. three.js r128 comes from cdnjs.

## Tools

- `tools/assets/` the Poly Haven pipeline: weld, simplify with meshoptimizer, drop foliage cards, pack every mesh into `assets/scan_pack.js` (gltf-transform). Paths in these scripts point at the original workspace and need adjusting.
- `tools/video/` how the comparison videos are made: `rec.js` records a seeded match frame by frame in headless Chromium, `interp.py` doubles the frame rate with optical flow, `compose.py` stacks two builds into a 1080x1920 video with labels.
- `tests/` Playwright scripts used while building: boot, a long AI vs AI match, performance, a full match to the victory screen, screenshot sets.

## Credits

- Code written by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), directed by [@0xInsiderf5](https://x.com/0xInsiderf5)
- 3D models and textures: [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com), CC0. See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md)
- [three.js](https://threejs.org) r128, MIT
- Fonts: IM Fell English SC, Spectral (Google Fonts, SIL Open Font License)

## License

Code is MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Poly Haven assets stay CC0.

ericyanpek/game-sample-corner-mart.readme:
# 街角便利店 · Corner Mart

一间可以在浏览器里经营三分钟的 3D 便利店。游戏代码和 Blender 生成脚本由 **GPT-6 Astra** 编写，全部可编辑的 3D 资产由 **Blender** 生成，最后用 TypeScript + Three.js 组装成可玩的游戏。

> A small browser management game. GPT-6 Astra writes the game code and the Blender generator scripts, Blender produces every editable 3D asset, and TypeScript + Three.js run the game. It uses no paid asset services, downloaded models or texture packs.

![新手引导](docs/images/01-guided.png)

## 玩法

开门前先看今天的客流和商品需求，再决定备货、升级和货架布局。营业 3 分钟后结算，还可以在完全相同的客流下重玩一次，比较两种策略的差别。

| 筹备：看需求、选主题 | 营业：顾客按清单拿货、排队结账 |
|---|---|
| ![筹备面板](docs/images/02-plan.png) | ![营业中](docs/images/03-busy.png) |
| **街坊：每位顾客的清单与心情** | **第一视角：站到收银台后面** |
| ![购物清单](docs/images/04-customer.png) | ![店员视角](docs/images/05-pov.png) |

- 三个营业主题：早餐日、炎热日和下班高峰。每个主题的需求曲线和店内光照都不同。
- 顾客带着购物清单逐件拿货，最后一次付清。缺货或排队太久，顾客会失望离开。
- 两个收银台。兼岗店员处理完手上的收银单就去补货；补货可以设为缺货优先、饮料优先或面包优先。
- 饮料架有三档：木架、带灯架、冷藏柜。布局有两套：通道优先和补货优先。
- 可以切到店员或任意一位顾客的第一视角。
- 结算时毛利和现金分开算，并逐条列出钱花在哪、顾客为什么离开。

![结算](docs/images/06-results.png)

## 快速开始

需要 Node.js 20.19+（或 22.12+），以及支持 WebGL 的浏览器。

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev        # http://127.0.0.1:9418/
npm test           # 逻辑测试
npm run build      # 输出静态站点到 dist/
npm run preview    # 本地预览构建结果
```

`dist/` 是纯静态文件，可以放到任意静态托管上。进度保存在浏览器的 localStorage 里，三个主题各存一份。右上角的「从头再来」会清空进度，清空前会确认。

## 用 GPT-6 Astra + Blender 做游戏

这个仓库真正想展示的是**开发方式**，游戏是这套方式的产物。

1. **人提需求，模型写生成脚本。** GPT-6 Astra 不直接"画"模型，而是编写 `assets/source/*.py`。这些脚本在后台运行的 Blender 里，用代码搭出店铺、货架、人物、货箱和告示牌。
2. **每个资产保留两份。** 一份是 `.blend` 源文件，可以在 Blender 里继续手工修改；另一份是去掉重复几何、给游戏运行用的 `.glb`。
3. **用规格文件对齐资产和代码。** `assets/specs/*.json` 记录挂点名（例如 `shelf.drinks`、`stop.drinks`）、尺寸和商品槽位。游戏加载模型时会核对这些接口，所以改了模型外观不会弄坏经营逻辑。
4. **用测试守住每一轮迭代。** 经营规则和渲染完全分开，模拟用固定时间步和固定随机种子，同样的输入每次都得到同样的结果。每次改动都要先通过逻辑测试。

想自己改一处模型，可以从这里开始（详见 [docs/blender-assets.md](docs/blender-assets.md)）：

> 打开 `drink-shelf-lit.blend`，只调整灯带颜色，保留 `shelf.drinks`、`stop.drinks` 和各个商品单元的接口；导出新的 GLB，确认外观变了，而经营进度不受影响。

## 目录结构

```text
src/              游戏代码（TypeScript）
  sim.ts            经营规则：库存、预留、订单、结账；不依赖 Three.js
  day.ts            营业日流程：筹备 → 营业 → 收尾 → 结算，以及同条件重玩
  navigation.ts     路径规划与人物避让
  view.ts           Three.js 场景：摆放 GLB、动画插值、点选与标注
  guided-tour.ts    新手引导
  first-person.ts   第一视角跟随
  main.ts           入口：连接界面、存档和游戏循环
tests/            逻辑测试（node:test + tsx）
public/assets/    运行时资源：GLB 模型和 WebP 预览图
assets/source/    Blender 源文件（.blend）和生成脚本（.py）
assets/specs/     资产接口规格，以及测试用的起始状态
scripts/          在后台调用 Blender 运行生成脚本的包装器，以及 GLB 修补脚本
docs/             架构说明、资产说明、README 截图
```

架构细节见 [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)。

## 技术栈

TypeScript 5.9 · Three.js 0.180 · Vite 7 · Blender 5.2 LTS（Python API）· Web Audio（音效由程序实时合成，不含音频文件）

## 已知局限

- 人物用刚性关节动画，没有 IK，也没有手指抓取。寻路只在平面上进行，人与人之间的避让用圆形近似。
- 数值是第一轮的候选值，还没有经过真实玩家测试。"能完成目标"、"账目对得上"和"玩起来有趣"是三件要分开验证的事。
- 资产脚本是一轮轮迭代写出来的，后一轮会打开前一轮保存的 `.blend` 接着改。所以单独运行某一个脚本，不等于从零重建全部资产。

## 许可

viktorkav/metal4-shooter.readme:
# Metal 4 Shooter — Star Kimi K3

Shooter de nave para macOS do canal [ViktorKav](https://www.youtube.com/@vkav), escrito em Swift com renderer nativo em Metal 4. Tem cenário procedural, esquadrões de inimigos, tiros, barrel roll e um chefe.

O jogo nasceu no experimento com o Kimi K3. Esta versão inclui a nave criada no Tripo Smart Mesh P2.0 e a integração feita com o GPT-6 Astra na sessão de 09/10/2026, para o vídeo **“Tripo: pedi uma nave pra colocar no meu jogo”**.

## Requisitos

- macOS 26 ou superior.
- GPU com suporte a Metal 4. Validação desta publicação feita em um Mac com Apple M4 Max.
- Xcode com SDK do macOS 26 ou superior e Swift 6.2 ou superior. Validação feita com Xcode 27 beta.

O projeto usa Swift Package Manager e frameworks do macOS, sem dependências externas. O modelo GLB e sua textura já estão incluídos em `Sources/StarFox/Resources/Ships/player.glb`.

## Compilar e jogar

```sh
git clone https://github.com/viktorkav/metal4-shooter.git
cd metal4-shooter

# Ajuste o caminho se o seu Xcode estiver instalado em outro lugar.
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app ./make_app.sh -c release
open StarFox.app
```

Se você usa o Xcode beta, troque o caminho por `/Applications/Xcode-beta.app`. O script também usa esse caminho por padrão quando `DEVELOPER_DIR` não está definido.

O `.app` gerado inclui o modelo e a textura; pode ser movido para outra pasta e executado sem a árvore de fontes. É uma compilação local, sem assinatura de distribuição ou notarização.

Para executar diretamente pelo SwiftPM:

```sh
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app swift run StarFox
```

## Controles

| Tecla | Ação |
|---|---|
| Setas ou WASD | Mover a nave |
| Espaço | Iniciar a partida e atirar |
| Z ou Shift | Barrel roll |
| Duplo toque para esquerda/direita | Barrel roll para esse lado |
| R | Reiniciar após vitória ou derrota |
| ⌘Q | Sair |

## Testes

```sh
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app swift test
```

Os testes existentes verificam o importador GLB, o arquivo real da nave, a textura, as dimensões, o pivô, a orientação e os pontos dos motores.

Para uma captura com o renderer do jogo:

```sh
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app swift run StarFox \
  --autopilot --godmode --seed 20261005 \
  --snapshot /tmp/metal4-shooter.ppm --frames 120
```

O modo `--snapshot` escreve **PPM/P6**. Outras opções do executável: `--autopilot`, `--godmode`, `--seed N`, `--exit-on-end` e `--test-gameover`.

## Código e nave

- `Game.swift`, `Rail.swift` e `Input.swift`: jogo, cenário e controles.
- `Renderer.swift` e `Shaders.swift`: renderer Metal 4, sombras e bloom.
- `GLBMeshLoader.swift` e `PlayerShipAsset.swift`: importação e calibração da nave.
- `HUD.swift`, `GameView.swift` e `AppDelegate.swift`: interface e janela do macOS.
- [Detalhes da integração da nave](docs/player-ship.md): formato suportado, escala, pivô, motores e textura.

O importador atende ao modelo estático desta demonstração; não cobre cenas glTF arbitrárias, animação, skinning ou compressão. A iluminação continua sendo a do jogo.

## Versão original

A tag [`shooter-original`](https://github.com/viktorkav/metal4-shooter/tree/shooter-original) preserva o shooter com a nave procedural, antes da integração com o Tripo.

```sh
git switch --detach shooter-original
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app ./make_app.sh
open StarFox.app
```

Para voltar à versão com a nave do Tripo, use `git switch main`.

# CHANNEL // SURF

An original, dependency-free retro arcade game with eight constantly changing genres. Run `npm start` and open http://localhost:5173.

Use arrows or WASD to move, Space for action, and Escape to pause. Mobile players have touch controls. Each channel switch briefly introduces the controls. Choose starting difficulty, speed acceleration, switch duration, and included genres on the splash screen. Select one genre for practice.

Modes: space shooter, endless runner, breakout, snake, racing, flappy flight, asteroids, and frogger. Score and lives continue between channels; speed increases through the run. Shooter, runner, Breakout, racing, flight, and Asteroids use survival timers, with no score quota. Snake and Frogger require untimed objectives to switch (on Arcade: 5 pickups or 3 crossings). Complete those targets without taking a hit: losing a life resets target progress, while overall score remains. Targets scale with difficulty, switch cadence, and later rounds. Idle objective play earns no survival points. Each Frogger crossing accelerates traffic. Survival rounds start with threats already in play, and runner jumps require individual presses. Scores are saved locally in the browser. Sound is synthesized with Web Audio, and all artwork is drawn in Canvas. Google Fonts are optional; system fonts are used offline.

`npm run check` checks syntax. `npm test` exercises all eight game engines, scoring, movement, collisions, pause, switching, acceleration, invulnerability, game over, and restart. Open `/?debug=1` for the developer-only `window.arcadeDebug` test controls.

The game runs directly from `index.html`, `arcade.css`, and `arcade.js`. No build step or runtime dependencies are required. `arcade-server.cjs` provides the local development server.

## High scores

Enter a player name before starting. Completed runs save automatically. The table shows the top 20 scores, with time, channels, difficulty, enabled genre count, speed ramp, and switch cadence. Shared and local tables retain their top 100 runs.

- On PHP hosting, `scores.php` saves the shared table on the server so everyone on that website sees the same leaderboard.
- Without PHP, the game falls back to a local table in browser storage. Scores and personal best survive closing and reopening the browser. Clearing site data, changing browsers, or ending a private browsing session removes or separates those local scores.
- Every run saves locally before attempting a shared submission. If the server is unavailable, the page says so and offers a retry for the latest run.

## PHP hosting

Upload `index.html`, `arcade.css`, `arcade.js`, `leaderboard.js`, and `scores.php` together to a PHP 8.1+ host. The PHP process must be able to create and write `score-data.php` in the game directory. The file is created automatically and starts with a PHP guard to prevent direct web access. It is excluded from Git: preserve it when deploying updates and include it in server backups. Alternatively, set `CHANNEL_SURF_SCORE_FILE` to a writable file path outside the public web directory.

For local PHP development, run `npm run start:php` and open http://localhost:5174. `npm start` runs a static Node server and exercises the browser-only fallback. The PHP development server is for local use; use your web host's PHP runtime for the public website.

`npm test` runs the gameplay checks plus shared-score API checks when PHP is installed, including persistence across server restarts, duplicate submissions, invalid input, and inaccessible storage. Submitted scores come from the browser and are not independently verified gameplay results.

---

The arcade includes two playable modes that share a unified **Persistent Sticker Toybox**:

1. **Magic Soup (`CAULDRON` Mode):**
   * **Summon a Hungry Guest:** Shout any character idea into the microphone (or tap a saved friend on the left shelf). Wave your hands over the **Magic Cloud** on the webcam mirror to wake them up!

2. **Flying Train (`FLYING_TRAIN` Mode):**
   * **AR Hand Steering:** Move your hands on the webcam mirror to steer a winged steam locomotive up and down through the sky.

# Opus FPS - A experiment with Opus 5.5 creating an old school looking Godot based FPS

![In game: a rocket sets off the gas cans at the outpost, throwing barrels into the air, with a demon and a floating eye nearby](docs/screenshot.jpg)

A first-person shooter with a PS1 look, made in Godot 4. Hunt floating eyes and electric rock golems across a hilly valley of pine groves, a village, an outpost and ruins. Blow up gas cans and barrels, collect gems and step through linked portals. Every model and sound is generated by scripts in `tools/`.

The game is in `godot/`. See [godot/README.md](godot/README.md) for how to run it, the controls and how the code fits together.

## PS1-style asset pack

![Showcase scene built from the pack](assets/previews/showcase.png)

The models in `assets/` are generated by `tools/generate_assets.py`. Preview images in `assets/previews/` are rendered by `tools/render_previews.py`. To regenerate, run:

```
B=/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender
$B -b --factory-startup -P tools/generate_assets.py -- assets   # models + palette
$B -b --factory-startup -P tools/render_previews.py -- assets   # preview images
```

### Previews

Each sheet shows every model with its name, triangle count and size. Single-model thumbnails are in `assets/previews/models/`.

![Terrain](assets/previews/sheet_terrain.png)
![Scenery](assets/previews/sheet_scenery.png)
![Weapons](assets/previews/sheet_weapons.png)
![Pickups](assets/previews/sheet_pickups.png)
![Enemies](assets/previews/sheet_enemies.png)
![Ammo](assets/previews/sheet_ammo.png)

### Palette

Every model uses one shared 128×64 texture, `assets/palette.png`. It is an 8×4 grid of 16 px swatches with a little pixel noise. Each face's UVs fall inside a single swatch, so every face reads as one flat color. Glowing parts (flames, pickups, eyes, keys) use a second material, `PS1_Glow`, which samples the same texture as emissive color. A portal's membrane uses a third material, `PS1_Portal`, meant to be replaced in the engine by an animated see-through shader. A creek's water uses a fourth, `PS1_Water`, meant to be replaced by a flowing-water shader. In other engines it shows as flat see-through blue-green.

| Row | Colors |
|-----|--------|
| Nature | `#1E2B1F` `#34452E` `#586B3E` `#4F4A2A` `#251B16` `#4A3628` `#8A7A5C` `#A89A7A` |
| Stone / wood | `#24262B` `#4A4D52` `#7A7A74` `#2E211A` `#5C4030` `#806248` `#5E2522` `#C8C4B8` |
| Water / metal | `#141F2B` `#2A4252` `#5C6E7A` `#1E2024` `#44484E` `#868C90` `#8C6E30` `#0C0C0C` |
| Accents | `#8E1A16` `#C85A1E` `#D6A83A` `#6FB83A` `#3FB6C4` `#4E2A6A` `#A8705F` `#BFB08C` |

The palette is deliberately somber: cold deep greens, muddy earth, heavy stone and dried-blood roofs. The saturated accent row is kept for blood, fire, pickups and energy weapons so they stand out.

The texture sampler is set to nearest filtering. For the full PS1 look, also turn off mipmaps in your engine (e.g. three.js `texture.generateMipmaps = false; texture.minFilter = NearestFilter`). Vertex snapping and affine texture warping are shader effects and belong in the engine, not in these files.

### Conventions (glTF, Y-up, meters)

- **assets/terrain/**: 8×8 m tiles with their origin at the center. Each tile's edges sit at height 0, so tiles placed on an 8 m grid connect seamlessly. `terrain_cliff` is an 8 m wall segment that tiles along X. `terrain_mountain` is a 30 m backdrop piece. `terrain_creek` carries a creek along X, so creek tiles chain end to end. The channel is about 4 m wide at the water line and 0.75 m deep, and meanders gently between grassy banks. It holds boulders on the banks, stones breaking the surface and pebbles on the gravel bed. Its water is a flat sheet 0.4 m down using a fourth material, `PS1_Water`, whose UVs are in meters with u running downstream (+X), so an engine shader can scroll ripples along the flow.
- **assets/scenery/**: origin at ground level. `fence_wood` is a 2 m segment with a post only at its -X end, so use `fence_post` to cap the last segment. `stone_wall` tiles every 4 m. Linwei-Chen/gpt-game-night-voyage.readme:
# 星筹夜航 · GPT 6.1 制作小游戏测试

用一副纸牌，找到自己的航线。组合牌型，让筹码与倍率增长，带着奇妙伙伴穿过八段夜航。

**[下载游戏](https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/gpt-game-night-voyage/releases/tag/v0.1.0) · [三分钟入门](docs/PLAYING.md) · [制作实验记录](docs/EXPERIMENT.md)**

[![自动检查](https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/gpt-game-night-voyage/actions/workflows/check.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/gpt-game-night-voyage/actions/workflows/check.yml)

![星筹夜航实战截图](docs/screenshots/03-playing.png)

这是一次“GPT 6.1 制作小游戏测试”，由 GPT / Codex 协作完成浏览器游戏。游戏采用原创夜航主题、卡面、名称和声音，规则与数值有独立的事实记录。当前版本为可玩实验版。

## 直接开始玩

从 **[下载版本](https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/gpt-game-night-voyage/releases/tag/v0.1.0)** 获取 `night-voyage-v0.1.0-web.zip`，解压后按包内 `START_HERE.txt` 启动本地游戏。也可按下方“本地运行”从源码启动。第一次进入会出现12章“新手航行课”。建议先练第四课“亲手选出一个对子”，再点“去开局”、选择最低难度并开始航行。手机和电脑均可游玩；随时点顶部“教程”复习。

每手选1～5张牌，组成对子、两对、顺子、同花等牌型。得分是最终筹码乘最终倍率，累加到本关总分。在出牌次数耗尽前达到目标就过关；缺关键牌时，用弃牌换牌。过关后去商店买伙伴、升级牌型和改造纸牌，再去下一关。

- **做出你的组合：**150名伙伴、12种牌型、15种起始牌组、8档难度。
- **边玩边学习：**选牌练习、逐步计分、伙伴顺序对比与利息滑块。
- **建立自己的牌组：**道具、凭单、印记、强化、版本与卡包。
- **继续挑战：**完成八段后获胜，也能继续同一局的更远航程。
- **适合反复尝试：**种子重现、自动存档、保存恢复、速度与减少运动设置。

存档保存在当前浏览器。同一种子、牌组、难度与操作可重现本游戏的一局；换浏览器或清除网站数据会影响本地存档。设置中可以导出存档。

## 想做第一局挑战？

先用最低难度通关第一段，试着用一个常出的牌型建立伙伴组合。觉得有趣，欢迎给仓库点个Star，分享你的种子、牌组、伙伴组合和最终成绩；也可在 [玩家讨论](https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/gpt-game-night-voyage/discussions) 交流玩法；遇到问题请用 [反馈模板](https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/gpt-game-night-voyage/issues/new/choose) 记录操作和截图。

![手机选牌教程](docs/screenshots/tutorial/05-practice-mobile.png)

## 本地运行

下载网页成品并解压后，在解压目录运行 `python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1`，再打开 <http://127.0.0.1:8080/>。Windows已安装Python时可将 `python3` 换成 `python`。

从源码运行需要Node.js 22或兼容版本。

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/gpt-game-night-voyage.git
cd gpt-game-night-voyage
npm ci
npm run dev
```

打开终端显示的网址。构建生产版使用 `npm run build`，预览使用 `npm run preview`。

## 制作与验证

采用TypeScript、PixiJS与Vite，逻辑与画面分离。计分使用事件队列，伙伴效果使用声明式注册器，随机序列可复现。完整实验过程、测试范围和观察结果见 [实验记录](docs/EXPERIMENT.md)。

```sh
npm test
npm run audit
npm run verify:facts
npm run verify:run
```

既有统一测试1,967项通过，包含行为场景和同源字段一致性检查；还有手算计分、24关正常实战、203步保存恢复重放、桌面/手机教程与独立评审。详细范围见 [验证报告](docs/verification-report.md)、[覆盖看板](docs/coverage.md) 和 [事实表](docs/fact-table.md)。自动检查会重新执行测试、构建、重放和项目子路径浏览器验证。

当前开放完整内容目录；持久解锁、挑战、成就尚未实现，完整无尽及原版整局/逐帧对照尚未验收。已有规则参考Balatro并做独立实现，最终1:1原版验收仍以验证报告中的缺口为准。

## 贡献与许可

欢迎完善玩法说明、改进手机操作、补充边界测试或分享有趣的种子。见 [贡献说明](CONTRIBUTING.md)。项目独立编写的代码与原创内容采用 [MIT许可](LICENSE)；Noto字体及其子集按OFL使用，依赖的许可见 [第三方记录](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

Leichtbier/living-greifswald.readme:
# Living Greifswald

Gemütliche, stilisierte three.js-Szenen aus Greifswald zum Herumlaufen in der Draufsicht.
Erster Ort: der **Fischmarkt mit dem Fischerbrunnen**, mit frechen Silbermöwen.

**Online spielen:** https://leichtbier.github.io/living-greifswald/
(GitHub Pages, Quelle: Branch `main`, Ordner `/`; `index.html` leitet nach `app/` weiter.)

## Starten
`app\start.bat` doppelklicken – öffnet `http://localhost:8080/app/` im Browser. Das Skript nimmt das erste Python, das wirklich läuft:
1. Umgebungsvariable `PYTHON` (z. B. `set PYTHON=%USERPROFILE%\.conda\envs\claude-code-env\python.exe`)
2. die conda-Umgebung `%USERPROFILE%\.conda\envs\claude-code-env`, falls vorhanden
3. `python` aus dem PATH (der Microsoft-Store-Platzhalter wird übersprungen)
4. der `py`-Launcher

Oder von Hand: `cd app` und `python serve.py 8080` (Python ≥ 3.7, nur Standardbibliothek; `--no-browser` unterdrückt den Browser).
three.js wird vom CDN (jsdelivr) geladen.

Steuerung: WASD/Pfeile laufen, Shift rennen, Q/E oder rechte Maustaste ziehen = Kamera drehen, Mausrad = Zoom,
N = Tag/Abend, G = einer Möwe folgen, H = Hilfe, B = Bearbeiten-Modus (siehe unten).

## Umgebung bearbeiten (B)
Im Bearbeiten-Modus (Taste `B` oder `?edit`) lassen sich Tische, Stühle, Schirme, Bänke, Laternen, Fahrräder, Autos,
Kübel, Mülleimer, Poller und die Skulpturen auswählen, verschieben, drehen, skalieren, kopieren und löschen:
- Klick wählt die oberste Ebene (z. B. Schirm mit seinen Tischen), ein weiterer Klick geht tiefer (Tisch → Stuhl),
  `Esc` eine Ebene höher, `Tab` zum nächsten Teil derselben Ebene (z. B. der Tisch unter dem Schirm).
- Ausgewähltes Teil mit der Maus über den Boden ziehen oder das Gizmo benutzen: `T` verschieben, `R` drehen, `V` Höhe;
  `Shift` rastet ein (10 cm / 15°). `+`/`-` (10 %) oder `Alt`+Mausrad (fein) ändern die Größe.
- `Strg+D` legt eine Kopie daneben, `Strg+C` und dann `Strg+V` fügt eine Kopie an der Mausposition ein.
- `Entf` löscht, `Pos1` setzt Lage, Drehung und Größe zurück, `Strg+Z` macht rückgängig.
- `Alt`+Klick auf eine beliebige Fläche setzt eine **Anmerkung für Claude** (Text, Stelle, Screenshot) → `model/annotations.json`.
  Beim nächsten Einbacken setzt Claude offene Anmerkungen um und markiert sie grün mit einer Antwort (Klick auf den Punkt).
- Jede Änderung speichert `serve.py` sofort in `model/edits.json`. Ohne lokalen Server (z. B. GitHub Pages) lädt `Strg+S` die Datei herunter.
- Die App wendet `edits.json` beim Laden an, auch wenn noch nicht neu gebaut wurde. Dauerhaft in die Modelle
  (inkl. Kollidern) kommt alles mit dem nächsten Blender-Build, siehe `model/README.md`.

## Aufbau
| Ordner | Inhalt |
|---|---|
| `app/` | Spiel: `index.html`, `main.js` (Szene, Figur, Kollision, Kamera), `seagulls.js` (Möwen-KI), `parts.js`/`editor.js` (Bearbeiten-Modus), `serve.py` |
| `app/tests/` | Playwright-Tests: `python app/tests/playwright_sim.py --out <ordner>` |
| `model/` | Exportierte Modelle (`*.glb`) und die Blender-Skripte, die sie erzeugen (siehe `model/README.md`) |

## Modelle neu bauen (Blender 5.1)
```
cd model
python make_textures.py
blender -b --factory-startup --python build_fischerbrunnen.py
blender -b --factory-startup --python build_seagull.py
```

## Tests
Benötigt `pip install playwright` und Microsoft Edge (wird über `channel="msedge"` genutzt, Rendering über die GPU).
Prüft Kollision, eine 300-s-Möwensimulation, Echtzeit-Spiel und Fluchtverhalten; Screenshots und `results.json` landen im `--out`-Ordner.

randy-jin/ai-minecraft-battle.readme:
# AI Minecraft 对决：Gemini 4 Argon vs GPT-6.1-sol

同一句提示词，让两个模型各写一个单文件、浏览器直接运行的 Minecraft 风格 3D 方块游戏，然后从**体验**和**架构**两个角度评测。

作者：[@RandyJinAI](https://x.com/RandyJinAI)。

## 在线试玩

- [Gemini 4 Argon 版](https://randy-jin.github.io/ai-minecraft-battle/gemini-4-argon.html)
- [GPT-6.1-sol 版](https://randy-jin.github.io/ai-minecraft-battle/gpt-6.1-sol.html)

也可以下载 HTML 文件后双击用浏览器打开（需联网加载 Three.js）。操作：点击画面锁定鼠标，WASD 移动，空格跳跃，左键挖方块，右键放方块，数字键 1-4 切换方块。

提示词原文见 [prompt.md](prompt.md)。两份代码均为模型原样输出，未做修改。

## 结论

**Gemini 4 Argon 体验更好，GPT-6.1-sol 架构更好。** 两份都能直接玩，题目要求全部做到。

| 评分（满分 10） | Gemini 4 Argon | GPT-6.1-sol |
|---|---|---|
| 需求完成度 | 9.5 | 9 |
| 体验 | 9 | 7 |
| 架构 | 6 | 8 |

## Gemini 4 Argon

**亮点**
- 音效、挖方块粒子、像素图标快捷栏、触屏按钮、暂停和重新生成地形
- 指针锁定失败时可按住鼠标拖动转视角，兼容性好
- 分 8 个编号章节，中文注释详细，适合学习

**问题**
- 每个方块一个独立 Mesh，约 5000 多个，绘制调用多，地图放大会卡
- 每帧遍历全部方块来做瞄准检测，开销随方块数线性增长
- 有一处注释写着"防止挖穿掉进虚空"，但代码里没有实现
- 树冠用草方块代替树叶；Three.js 版本较旧（r128）

## GPT-6.1-sol

**亮点**
- 只渲染至少一面外露的方块，按类型合批为 InstancedMesh，约 5 次绘制调用
- 地图 56×56，是 Argon 版（29×29）的 3 倍多
- 碰撞用小步推进加二分修正，物理按固定子步更新，基本不会穿墙
- 数据（一个 Map）与渲染分离，结构干净

**问题**
- 每挖或放一个方块，都把整个世界重建一遍，地图越大越卡
- 瞄准检测对 InstancedMesh 逐实例计算，实测帧率约为 Argon 版的三分之一（软件渲染环境，仅供相对比较）
- 指针锁定前所有按键无响应，在不允许锁定的环境里无法游玩

## 两份都没做到的三件事

体素游戏的标准优化，也是"能跑"和"能上线"的区别：

1. **按区块（chunk）合并几何体**：修改一个方块只重建所在区块
2. **隐藏面剔除**：被相邻方块挡住的面不生成
3. **体素网格射线遍历（DDA）**：瞄准检测只走几格，开销与世界大小无关

## 截图

| Gemini 4 Argon | GPT-6.1-sol |
|---|---|
| ![](screenshots/gemini-4-argon.png) | ![](screenshots/gpt-6.1-sol.png) |

## Original Prompts

### Initial Prompt
> create the ultimate brutalist city builder. you should have lots of controls over buildings in ways that are delightful and inuitive to people who just want to play, but are sophisticated and deep for people who know something about architecture. you should be able to play a lot with design and approach. there should be simulation modes and different ways to view or experience the city. make it stunning. i want to host this on netlify in the end

## Quick Start & Netlify Deployment Recipes

### 1. Run Locally (Development Server)
```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run dev
```

### 2. Build Production Bundle (`dist/`)
```bash
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm run build
pnpm run preview
```

### 3. Deploy to Netlify
This project includes a pre-configured [`netlify.toml`](./netlify.toml) (`command = "pnpm run build"`, `publish = "dist"`).

#### Option A: Netlify CLI (Instant Deploy)
```bash
pnpm dlx netlify-cli deploy --build --prod
```
*(Note: Use Safari when authenticating with Netlify in the browser.)*

#### Option B: Drag & Drop `dist/` Folder
1. Run `pnpm run build`
2. Drag the generated `dist/` folder directly into [app.netlify.com/drop](https://app.netlify.com/drop).

---

## Architectural Features & Controls

### 10 Iconic Brutalist Building Archetypes
- **ARC-01 // Unité d'Habitation** (*Le Corbusier, 1952*): Radiant slab elevated on muscular V-shaped pilotis, deep egg-crate brise-soleil duplex loggias, and sculptural rooftop ventilation chimneys.
- **ARC-02 // Habitat 67 Cluster** (*Moshe Safdie, 1967*): Interlocking cantilevered precast voxel modules with rooftop botanical gardens.
- **ARC-03 // Barbican Estate Tower** (*Chamberlin, Powell & Bon, 1976*): Bush-hammered coarse granite tower with sawtooth balcony bands and triple barrel-vaulted crowns.
- **ARC-04 // Inverted Civic Ziggurat** (*Kallmann McKinnell & Knowles, 1968*): Boston City Hall tribute with cantilevered deep-coffered upper tiers stepping outward above an open civic forum.
- **ARC-05 // Metabolist Capsule Core** (*Kisho Kurokawa, 1972*): Twin slip-formed service cores with plug-in cantilevered porthole capsules.
- **ARC-06 // Geisel Cantilever Crown** (*William Pereira, 1970*): 45° diagonal post-tensioned concrete tree bents supporting cantilevered octagonal reading tiers.
- **ARC-07 // Trellick Skybridge Slab** (*Ernő Goldfinger, 1972*): Razor-thin residential block connected every third story by flying skybridges to a detached lift and boiler tower.
- **ARC-08 // Salk Horizon Court** (*Louis Kahn, 1965*): Symmetrical pozzolanic concrete and travertine study wings angled at 45° flanking a central equatorial water channel.
- **ARC-09 // Yugoslav Spomenik** (*Živković & Bogdanović, 1971*): Radial crystalline concrete petals soaring outward from a stepped ceremonial amphitheater.
- **ARC-10 // Sunken Water Forum** (*Lawrence Halprin / Barbican, 1974*): Stepped concrete basin with reflecting pool, cypress planters, and brutalist plaza sculpture.

### 4 Real-Time Urban Simulation Modes
1. **01 SOLAR HELIODON**: Interactive 3D sun-path dome (Summer Solstice, Vernal Equinox, Winter Solstice) + facade solar insolation vs. brise-soleil shading efficiency heatmap.
2. **02 STREETS IN THE SKY**: Autonomous ground flâneurs, vertical core elevators, and elevated skybridge pedestrian flows with Space Syntax connectivity metrics.
3. **03 VENTURI WIND TUNNEL**: Animated 3D aerodynamic streamlines demonstrating how Le Corbusier *pilotis* liberate ground-level airflow compared to solid canyon blocks.
4. **04 STRUCTURAL LOAD PATH**: Finite-element compression and cantilever tension stress visualization across cores, pilotis piers, and overhangs.

### 4 Camera Views & 4 Monograph Rendering Styles
- **Camera Modes**: Perspective Orbit, True Parallel Orthographic Axonometric, First-Person 1.7m Flâneur Walk (`WASD` + mouse look + Ground Plaza vs. Elevated Skybridge toggle), and Autonomous Drone Tour.
- **Live 3D Section Cut**: Slice through the entire city along the `X-Axis`, `Z-Axis`, or `Horizontal Plan Cut` in real time.
- **Visual Styles**: Photoreal *Béton Brut*, *Lucien Hervé* High-Contrast 1950s B&W Photography, *Cyanotype* Technical Blueprint, and *Museum Clay Maquette*.

# The Vertical Lost & Found

[English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b126354c-ce20-4bfc-b07f-9eb815dfc5b7

[Download the original 1080p60 video](showcase-1080p60.mp4)

Built with **Gemini 4 in Google Antigravity**, using Nano Banana texture imagery, Blender and Three.js.

A climbing puzzle inside a railway archive. Pull drawers along their rails, lock them into place and move luggage to drive the lifts. Three stages lead from the first drawer to a rooftop garden.

This is a development build shared for review. The mechanics work through the saved routes, but the character, repeated cabinetry and lighting still fall short of the photographic target. Full motion, listening and audiovisual sync review remain unperformed.

## Build prompt

Copy the complete prompt in your preferred language: [English](prompts/en.md) · [简体中文](prompts/zh-CN.md) · [한국어](prompts/ko.md) · [日本語](prompts/ja.md).

These are equivalent versions of a consolidated brief for rebuilding the experience with Gemini 4, Nano Banana, Blender and Three.js. The project took multiple iterations; a prompt cannot guarantee identical generated assets or results. To run this exact implementation, use the committed source and assets below. The [prompt guide](prompts/README.md) also includes the original English brief and explains the difference between the visual target and this build.

## Run locally

Use Node.js 20 or newer. No API key is needed to play.

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open the local URL printed by Vite. For the production build:

```sh
npm run build
npm run preview
```

## Controls

| Control | Action |
|---|---|
| W A S D | Move |
| Space | Jump |
| Tab / Shift + Tab | Select a reachable mechanism / cargo |
| Q / E | Push / pull the selected rail |
| L | Lock or release a rail notch |
| H | Open or close a cargo hatch |
| F | Pick up, place or dispatch cargo |
| G | Open the final drawer from inside |
| R | Restore the latest checkpoint |

The in-game hints explain the selected target. Sound starts after an interaction and can be muted.

## Verify and edit

```sh
npm run verify
```

This builds the application and runs 77 mechanics checks plus four ordinary-control routes. Generated test evidence goes into `.run/verification/`. Human difficulty testing remains separate.

Editable `.blend` files are in `assets/blender/`. Geometry builders, raw generated textures, material preparation scripts and the persistent scene records are included. See [authoring](docs/authoring.md), [recording](docs/recording.md) and [verification](docs/verification.md).

The one-minute showcase contains 3,600 simulation samples at 1920 × 1080 with stereo audio. It was captured offline through the actual game controls. The separate replay benchmark measured 37.33 renders/s on the tested machine; that is not a full live-play FPS result.

The project uses a constrained character/support controller and analytic mechanisms, with discrete cargo pickup and placement. It is not a general rigid-body simulator.

# Lumencraft

A voxel sandbox that runs in the browser. There is one persistent world and everyone who opens the page plays in it together.

**Play:** https://testyee-09.github.io/opus5.5Minecraft/

- Infinite procedural worlds: 14 biomes, rivers, caves, lush caves, ores, and **floating sky islands** with waterfalls and glowing crystal ore
- Shader-pack look out of the box: real-time sun and moon shadows, screen-space water reflections, bloom, god rays, smooth lighting, waving foliage, fog and an atmospheric sky with clouds, stars, shooting stars and auroras
- Survival: health, hunger, drowning, fall damage, mining tiers, crafting with a recipe book, furnaces, chests, farming, beds, TNT, bows
- Mobs: pigs, cows, sheep, chickens; zombies and skeletons that burn at dawn; spiders
- Flowing water and lava, falling sand, leaf decay, crop growth, weather with thunderstorms
- One shared world: no rooms or codes. A Cloudflare Durable Object (`server/`) stores every block edit, chest, furnace and player save, and relays messages; the longest-connected player's browser runs the simulation and hands it over when they leave
- If the server can't be reached you can play an offline copy of the world
- Character creator, generative piano soundtrack, recorded sound effects

Everything visual (textures, models, terrain) is generated in code. See `public/CREDITS.md` for audio credits.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

World server: `cd server && npx wrangler@4.151.0 deploy` (wss://lumencraft-world.nomaeofficial.workers.dev/world).

# Starwing

A tiny Star Fox (SNES)-inspired rail shooter, made with Bevy 0.20.0 and original procedural geometry. No Nintendo assets or textures. Includes an original Blender-built panther comms portrait.

## Run

```sh
cd starwing # from the parent bevy directory
cargo run
```

`rust-toolchain.toml` selects Rust 1.99.0 (Bevy requires at least 1.97.1) and includes the WebAssembly target. Rustup installs this toolchain automatically without changing your global default. The first build downloads and compiles Bevy; expect several minutes. Native builds use Metal (macOS), Vulkan, or DirectX 12.

## Neon Sprawl

Fly down a cyan/magenta grid highway between scrolling triangulated wireframe mountains, under a striped orange-to-pink sun, violet sunset gradient, and stars. Obstacles stay inside the playable lane; decorative mountains remain outside it. The scenery uses shared unlit vertex-color materials and ordinary triangle ribbons, not native polygon-mode wireframe, custom shaders, or desktop-only post-processing.

For a WebGL2-compatible compile check:

```sh
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features web
```

## Web build / FTP upload

```sh
./build-web.sh
```

This produces `dist/` and `starwing-web.zip`. Extract the ZIP locally and upload **its contents** (`index.html`, `starwing.js`, `starwing_bg.wasm`) by FTP into any public folder, for example `public_html/games/starwing/`. Open `https://your-domain.example/games/starwing/` and click **Play Starwing**. All URLs are relative, so no domain or subfolder configuration is needed. The game assets and music are embedded in WASM.

Use a modern desktop browser with WebGL2 and a keyboard. Serve over HTTP(S), not by opening `index.html` directly from disk. No server-side code, routing rules, cross-origin isolation headers, or WASM MIME configuration is required. Browser sound may need a click after loading. Upload the three files together when updating (and refresh the browser cache). The script installs the matching `wasm-bindgen` CLI if needed; the initial release build takes several minutes. Web builds use a separate size-optimized profile with link-time optimization and omit debugging names. If Binaryen is installed (`brew install binaryen` on macOS), the script also runs `wasm-opt -Os`. Native build settings are unchanged. Enable gzip/Brotli on your web host if available to reduce download sizes further; the ZIP is only an upload archive.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| WASD / arrows | Steer |
| Hold Space | Twin lasers |
| Left / right Shift | Barrel roll: brief immunity, 3-second cooldown |
| P | Pause / resume |
| R | Restart anytime |
| Esc | Quit |

Survive the 90-second canyon run. Shoot red fighters for 100 points each; avoid their aimed shots, floating rocks, and walls with narrow openings. Five shield hits end the run. Damage briefly makes you invulnerable (the ship flashes). Obstacles cannot be destroyed. Chromatic aberration is always visible, with exaggerated color splitting on hits. Hits briefly shake the camera: laser impacts are subtle, shield damage is stronger, and crashes/destruction give the largest jolt. Hit effects fade back to the resting camera and baseline aberration, freeze while paused, and reset on restart; immune hits do not trigger damage feedback. The course gets faster and waves more frequent as you progress.

## Panther comms monitor

A live 3D panther portrait sits in a bottom-left monitor with CRT scanlines and a slow scanning band. Kills and rolls trigger a smile; shield hits trigger hurt/fear, with a stronger caption at two shields or fewer; victory celebrates and defeat holds the hurt pose. Expressions ease back to neutral between events. Damage takes priority over kill feedback. Pause freezes reactions and restart clears them. Talking is disabled.

The model renders to a 256×256 image on an isolated layer, then into the UI; it cannot appear in the flight scene. The render target uses sRGB directly without alternate texture views, and portrait point lights preserve WebGL2's single directional-light budget. Scanlines use ordinary UI strips, with no custom shader. The GLB is embedded for native and web. Controls sit in the bottom right to avoid the monitor.

Record the seven lines listed in [`assets/voice/panther/README.md`](assets/voice/panther/README.md), put the named WAVs in that directory, and rebuild. Optional clips are embedded automatically. Missing clips remain silent; captions still work. Voice playback is rate-limited, pauses with the game, and urgent cues interrupt less important lines. No lip-sync is enabled.

## Soundtrack

The supplied ProTracker MOD **Space Walk** is preserved at `assets/music/ace_fi_-_space_walk.mod` and embedded in the executable. `xmrs` / `xmrsplayer` import its instruments, patterns, and effects and render one complete pass to stereo PCM in memory at startup. Bevy loops that audio at 25% volume beneath the sound effects. No

# 五模型五題橫評 (2026-10-14)

> **本測試為 Oneshot 式測試**：每個模型每一題只作答一次，送出 prompt 後直接收下第一份輸出，中途沒有追問、提示、修正或重跑，也沒有挑選較好的一次。結果反映的是「一次到位」的表現，同一模型多跑幾次可能得到不同答案。

同一組五道實務題 (CG 明信片設計、email 書寫、學測作文、經費配平、時事評論)，分別交給五個模型作答，再比較作答品質、事實正確性與成本。

**線上瀏覽：** [展示頁](https://ag-0814.github.io/261014_LLM-Oneshot-Test/) (每個模型每一題的作答、思考過程、原始回應、明信片都可直接點開) · [AI 比較報告](https://ag-0814.github.io/261014_LLM-Oneshot-Test/%E6%B8%AC%E8%A9%A6%E7%B5%90%E6%9E%9C/%E6%AF%94%E8%BC%83%E5%A0%B1%E5%91%8A/index.html)

|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Opus 5.5 | Claude Code 子代理 | `prompt_App.txt` | 讀檔、上網、執行程式 |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | Claude Code 子代理 | `prompt_App.txt` | 讀檔、上網、執行程式 (PDF 無法轉圖，作文題改用文字擷取) |
| Gemini 4 Argon | OpenRouter API | `prompt_API.txt` | 無 |
| Muse Wonder | OpenRouter API | `prompt_API.txt` | 無 |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | OpenRouter API | `prompt_API.txt` | 無 (第二輪補測) |

思考強度一律設為 medium。數字以程式重算，事實對照新聞原文。另外補測了 Sonnet 5.5 走 OpenRouter API 的 CG 明信片題 (`sonnet-5.5_API`)，未列入總結表。

## AI 評分總結

| 數學配平 | 優 | 待定 | 弱 | 優 | 良 |

## 人類排序 vs AI 評分

AI 評分來自上方比較報告；人類排序來自評審的主觀閱讀 ([評價全文](測試結果/比較報告/用戶主觀橫評.md))。名次相同表示並列，兩者都只在同一題內比較。

| 題目 | Opus 5.5 | Sonnet 5.5 | Gemini 4 Argon | Muse Wonder | GPT-6.1 Sol |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CG 明信片 | **#1** · 優 | #2 · 良 | #4 · 優 | #6 · 可 | #3 · 良 |

格式為「人類名次 · AI 評分」。人類排序原文 (`>` 越多代表差距越大)：

| 題目 | 人類排序 |
|---|---|
| CG 明信片 | O5.5 > So5.5 >> Sol6.1 > G4A = So5.5_API > Mu2 |

對照下來的幾個差異：

- **一致的地方**：Opus 5.5 在明信片與作文兩邊都拿第一；Sonnet 5.5 的 email 兩邊都墊底 (注音錯誤、措辭不妥)。

- **明信片題的 Gemini 4 Argon**：AI 評「優」(版面元素最完整)，人類排第四，理由正是元素堆太滿、不做取捨。

# Vanilla 3D rendering with Gemini 4 Argon

Written by Gemini 4 Argon, the repository includes two self-contained engines that build a sunlit concrete and walnut library from first principles. The first is an offline renderer written in Python and NumPy. The second is a real-time browser engine built with vanilla JavaScript and WebGL2 that reshapes the room as you resize the frame.

![Sunlit concrete and walnut library](renders/sunlit_library_1600x1200.png)

## Repository structure

The project is organized into two self-contained folders. Each folder can be inspected or run on its own without external assets.

| Folder | Contents | Entry point |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| python | Python and NumPy offline ray tracer | python/sunlit_library.py |
| javascript | Interactive resizable vanilla JavaScript and WebGL2 scene | javascript/index.html |

## Running the live WebGL2 room

The interactive scene runs directly in any modern browser with WebGL2 support and needs no build step, bundler, or external library.

Start a local web server from the root of the repository so the browser can load the page cleanly:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Once the local server is running, open http://localhost:8000/javascript/index.html in your web browser.

Dragging the bottom-right corner or edges of the frame reshapes the room in real time on the graphics card. The walls, window bays, furniture spacing, and sun angle all adapt to fit the new frame proportions.

## Running the Python and NumPy renderer

Install the required NumPy and Pillow packages inside a Python virtual environment before running the offline renderer:

```bash
pip install -r python/requirements.txt
```

Render the standard 1600 by 1200 architectural photograph, which saves to renders/sunlit_library_1600x1200.png by default when no custom path is given:

```bash
python3 python/sunlit_library.py
```

Pass the widescreen flag to render a 16:9 panoramic edition at 1920 by 1080 pixels in the same output folder:

```bash
python3 python/sunlit_library.py --16x9
```

You can also render at any custom pixel resolution and output path using environment variables and a filename argument:

```bash
PAINT_WIDTH=800 PAINT_HEIGHT=600 python3 python/sunlit_library.py output/preview.png
```

## How the room is laid out

The room sits inside a three-dimensional coordinate system measured in meters. In the table below, X measures width from left to right, Y measures height from floor to ceiling, and Z measures depth away from the camera.

| Element | World bounds | Material and geometry |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

## How light and materials are computed

Both the Python renderer and the WebGL2 browser engine build the image through seven physical steps. Each step solves one part of how light travels through a real room:

- Ray tracing follows one viewing ray per pixel from the camera into the room until it hits a geometric shape such as a box, cylinder, sphere, or curved page.
- Surface normals are tiny 3D tilt vectors that perturb each hit point to carve wood pores, travertine pits, wool loops, and timber grain without storing polygon meshes.
- Ambient occlusion darkens tight crevices where bookshelves, chair runners, and the table base block surrounding daylight from reaching the floor.
- Radiosity simulates how warm light from the sun and brass wall lamps bounces off oiled oak floorboards and walnut shelves to fill shadowed corners.
- Anisotropic reflections trace secondary rays from the floor and stretch bright window glare along the length of each oak board, matching real wood fibers.

# Carom

A browser paddle duel about angles and momentum. Strike while moving to curve the ball, bank shots off two amber obstacles, and reach 11 with a two-point lead. Play against the computer in Solo or share a keyboard in Versus.

Everything is drawn and synthesized in code. The game runs locally, without accounts, a backend, external assets, or runtime network requests.

## Run

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open the development URL printed by Vite.

```sh
npm run build
npm run preview
```

The production site is in `dist/`. Serve that directory at the root of any static web server.

## Controls

| Action | Controls |
| --- | --- |
| Solo paddle | W / S or ↑ / ↓ |
| Versus left paddle | W / S |
| Versus right paddle | ↑ / ↓ |
| Select menu item | W / S or ↑ / ↓; mouse or touch |
| Confirm | Enter / Space; click or tap |
| Pause / resume | P / Escape |
| Return from instructions | Escape |
| Toggle sound | M |
| Diagnostic overlay | Backtick |

Touch controls appear when you touch the screen. Motion at paddle contact adds spin; the ball's trail shows the resulting curve. Amber obstacles are solid, the top and bottom reflect, and the side edges score.

## Verification

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run format
npm test
```

Tests run the Simple 2D engine over a native canvas and controlled clocks, exercising menus, input, physics, serving, scoring, AI, and debug poses. The simulation builds a new state every frame; rendering and diagnostics only read it. Automation is available through `engine.debug` and `engine.apply` when constructing an engine with the exported `game`.

The player description, screenshots, and engine-recorded rally are in `showcase/`.
